description.value: The study investigated whether three weeks of inhibitory control training transfers to neural activation during an untrained emotion regulation task.

spans.text: The goal of this study is to investigate whether IC training transfers from a non-affective training task to an untrained affective task and to use neuroimaging to characterize the mechanism of transfer (or non-transfer).

value: we do predict changes in IC neural networks during the ER task as a result of IC training, specifically in the rIFG and possibly other regions

spans.text: However, we do predict changes in IC neural networks during the ER task as a result of IC training, specifically in the rIFG and possibly other regions that will provide evidence for or against the plausible mechanisms of training transfer described above.

spans.text: The instruction screen was followed by a neutral or negative International Affective Picture System (IAPS) picture (5000 ms), a blank screen (500 ms) and a prompt for participants to rate their distress on a Likert scale of 0–9 (4500 ms).

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to look and let themselves respond naturally, decrease emotion by reappraising the picture, or describe the scene.

spans.text: At the beginning of each block, participants were given one of three instructions (3000 ms): ‘look and let yourself respond naturally’ (Look), ‘decrease emotion’ (Reappraise) or ‘scene description’ (Label).

value: Distress ratings on a 0–9 Likert scale
ER score calculated as average distress on Look trials minus average distress on Reappraise trials
Comparison of Look versus Reappraise distress ratings to verify successful emotion regulation

spans.text: Behavioral measures of interest included ER scores calculated from the ER task distress ratings (i.e. the average distress rating on Look trials minus that on Reappraise trials averaged across both runs; greater scores indicated more effective ER)

description.value: An inhibitory control task with go trials and auditory stop-signal trials requiring participants to inhibit their button press.

instructions.value: Participants pressed the corresponding arrow key in response to the go signal and inhibited their button press when an auditory stop signal occurred.

stimuli.value: Left- or right-pointing arrows and auditory stop signals
